question: Why must you never leave a set-up sterile field unattended on the ward?

options.A: Because sterile drapes automatically fold up after five minutes
options.B: Because the sterile items will melt if exposed to room air
options.C: Because someone might contaminate it without your knowledge
options.D: Because hospital regulations fine nurses who walk away from trays

explanation: Spot on! If you walk away, someone might unknowingly brush against it or contaminate it, ruining your sterile setup. Stay close to your work!

question: Why should you use a clean spatula or tongue depressor when taking cream from a shared jar?

options.A: To spread the cream faster across the patient's skin
options.B: To measure the exact milligram dose required
options.C: To warm the cream up before touching the patient
options.D: To prevent introducing bacteria and contaminating the jar

explanation: Using a tool instead of your bare fingers stops germs from getting into the shared jar and causing future infections.

question: Why do community nurses still use paper records and stationery instead of computers all the time?

options.A: Community outposts often lack reliable computer networks and digital infrastructure
options.B: Paper forms are legally required to be more accurate than digital files
options.C: Rural patients refuse to let nurses use computers near them
options.D: Computers cannot store health data related to immunization

explanation: Spot on! Because remote health posts and home visits rarely have steady electricity or internet, good old paper remains our most practical tool.

question: A patient develops sudden severe shortness of breath, restlessness, and absent breath sounds on the treated side after a thoracocentesis. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Administer a mild oral pain medication and check vital signs in one hour
options.B: Remove the dressing and apply warm compresses to the puncture site
options.C: Encourage the patient to take slow, deep breaths to clear the airways
options.D: Notify the provider immediately and prepare for a chest tube insertion

explanation: Absent breath sounds and severe shortness of breath point to a significant pneumothorax or lung collapse, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is the very first step in newborn resuscitation if a baby doesn't cry or breathe right after birth?

options.A: Dry thoroughly with warm towels and provide stimulation
options.B: Administer emergency intravenous drugs through the umbilical cord
options.C: Submerge the baby briefly in warm water to shock the system
options.D: Give chest compressions at a rate of 120 beats per minute

explanation: Drying and rubbing the baby warms them up and gives just enough stimulation to get them breathing on their own.

question: What does the letter 'C' stand for in the popular CAGE alcohol screening tool?

options.A: Craving
options.B: Control
options.C: Chronic
options.D: Cut down

explanation: The 'C' stands for asking if the patient has ever felt they ought to Cut down on their drinking. It's a quick, friendly way to start a health chat.

question: Which global region currently has the highest number of maternal deaths?

options.A: North America
options.B: Southeast Asia
options.C: Sub-Saharan Africa
options.D: Western Europe

explanation: As future Nigerian nurses, knowing our local context is key. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the heaviest load of maternal mortality, making our work so important.

question: A patient wants to bake a healthier cake with less refined sugar. What is a great nursing suggestion?

options.A: Use mashed ripe bananas or unsweetened applesauce to add natural sweetness and moisture
options.B: Add artificial chemical cleaners to make the dough rise faster
options.C: Double the amount of salt to block the bitter taste of unsweetened flour
options.D: Replace sugar with extra drops of liquid vegetable oil

explanation: Mashed fruits are fantastic baking substitutes! They bring natural sweetness and moisture thanks to their intrinsic sugars and fiber, keeping the cake delicious without refined sugar.

question: Which of these is NOT a current challenge facing community health nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Funding shortages for public health programs
options.B: Infrastructural deficits in rural clinics
options.C: The double burden of infectious and non-communicable diseases
options.D: Zero prevalence of any health problems in the country

explanation: You got it! Nigeria definitely still deals with various health challenges, so saying there are zero problems isn't true.

question: Which of these is NOT a good trait for a rehabilitation goal?

options.A: It is kept completely vague so staff can change it anytime
options.B: It includes a specific deadline for completion
options.C: It focuses on clear, trackable outcomes
options.D: It is planned together with the patient

explanation: Good goals are never vague! They need to be specific and measurable so everyone knows what they are working toward.

question: Which of these is a major barrier to nursing research in busy hospitals?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time during shifts
options.B: Too many available financial grants and computers
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and staffing shortages
options.D: Strict bans on publishing local healthcare data

explanation: Spot on! When nurse-to-patient ratios are high and everyone is exhausted, it's really tough to find the energy or time for research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: During a community disease outbreak, what is one of the main duties of a nurse?

options.A: Manufacturing new vaccines in the local clinic
options.B: Conducting contact tracing and health education
options.C: Prescribing experimental drugs without supervision
options.D: Changing national health budget allocations

explanation: As a nurse, you are a community educator and detective! You track down contacts and teach families how to stay safe and stop the spread.

question: On a standard muscle strength scale, what does a score of zero (0) indicate?

options.A: A slight flicker of movement only
options.B: No movement or muscle contraction at all
options.C: Movement is possible against gravity
options.D: Normal strength against full resistance

explanation: A score of zero means there is total paralysis or no visible muscle movement when the patient tries to move.

question: As a nurse, why should you explore a patient's cultural practices rather than just banning them?

options.A: Traditional practices replace the need for all modern antibiotic treatments
options.B: Patients are more likely to ignore advice that completely dismisses their traditional beliefs
options.C: Cultural practices are always scientifically proven to be beneficial for health
options.D: Hospital policies legally require nurses to perform traditional steam baths

explanation: Spot on! When we respect our patients' beliefs instead of judging them, they trust us more and are way more likely to listen to our health advice.

question: A nurse notices that many clients referred for long-acting methods never arrive at the general hospital. What practical step can she take to improve follow-up?

options.A: Increase the price of family planning commodities at her clinic
options.B: Scold clients publicly during clinic meetings for failing to travel
options.C: Stop referring clients altogether and attempt the procedures at the primary post
options.D: Engage community health workers to counsel and track referred clients

explanation: Community health workers can visit clients at home to address fears, answer questions, and encourage them to complete their referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)

question: Why does poor nutrition make HIV progress faster?

options.A: It causes instant resistance to antibiotics
options.B: It destroys the outer shell of the virus
options.C: It stops the liver from handling water
options.D: It further weakens the body's natural defenses

explanation: You got it! Without proper nutrients, the immune system simply doesn't have the fuel it needs to keep the virus in check.

question: Why do blood vessels become more permeable during the early stages of acute inflammation?

options.A: To allow protective fluid and white blood cells to enter the tissue
options.B: To cause immediate clotting and seal off the skin surface
options.C: To flush harmful bacteria directly back into the major arteries
options.D: To prevent any blood from reaching the injured site

explanation: Increased permeability lets immune cells and proteins escape the bloodstream to fight the infection at the tissue level. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which clinical sign will immediately make a doctor or nurse think of ordering a liver function panel?

options.A: Frequent coughing
options.B: Painful urination
options.C: Jaundice
options.D: Swollen ankles from heart failure

explanation: Spot on! That yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice) tells us bilirubin isn't clearing properly, making LFTs a top priority.

question: What causes the microfilariae to leave the skin sample and enter the liquid?

options.A: Active migration of the living parasites into the fluid
options.B: Electrical current passed directly through the glass vial
options.C: Chemical digestion of skin cells by strong laboratory acids
options.D: Mechanical centrifugation at high speeds in the machine

explanation: Well done! The living parasites actively wiggle and crawl out of the skin tissue into the surrounding water or saline.

question: Which layer of the epidermis is busy making new skin cells and producing melanin for color?

options.A: Stratum basale
options.B: Stratum corneum
options.C: Stratum granulosum
options.D: Stratum spinosum

explanation: You got it! The stratum basale is the deepest layer of the epidermis where cell division happens constantly, and special cells called melanocytes make our skin pigment.

question: What is the main reason for doing a medication review during a home visit after a hospital discharge?

options.A: To throw away all old medications so the client can buy new ones
options.B: To let the family decide which pills the client should swallow
options.C: To increase the total number of daily prescription drugs
options.D: To compare hospital discharge orders with what the client is actually taking

explanation: Spot on! Medication reconciliation clears up any confusion so the client takes the exact right drugs safely.

question: A patient becomes dizzy and nauseated shortly after taking a sublingual tablet. What unique advantage of this route can the nurse utilize?

options.A: Give a large glass of milk to neutralize the medicine.
options.B: Instruct the patient to spit out any remaining undissolved medication.
options.C: Wait for the liver to filter out the toxic portion.
options.D: Pump the patient's stomach immediately to remove the drug.

explanation: Because absorption happens in the mouth, removing unabsorbed medication can stop further entry into the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: Why are healthcare-associated infections a major concern in nursing?

options.A: They prolong hospital stays and increase patient suffering
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for antibiotics
options.C: They only affect nurses who fail to wear gloves
options.D: They are caused exclusively by patient diet changes

explanation: Infections acquired during healthcare delivery add heavy burdens to patients by worsening their health and lengthening their recovery time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which eye condition is an absolute contraindication for anticholinergic medications?

options.A: Conjunctivitis
options.B: Cataracts
options.C: Color blindness
options.D: Glaucoma

explanation: Anticholinergics dilate the pupil, which can trap fluid inside the eye and dangerously worsen glaucoma. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is the main transmission route for most water-borne pathogens?

options.A: The fecal-oral route
options.B: Skin contact with soil
options.C: Direct airborne droplets
options.D: Mosquito bite vectors

explanation: Water-borne diseases spread when microscopic fecal matter contaminates drinking or food preparation water, which is then swallowed. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h4)

question: A female patient keeps missing her medication pickups and acts very anxious whenever her husband is mentioned. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Complete indifference to her personal physical wellbeing
options.B: Potential gender-based control or financial dependency affecting care
options.C: An allergic reaction to the prescribed drug packaging
options.D: A simple case of mild seasonal forgetfulness

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Anxiety and missed visits can be red flags for controlling relationships or a lack of financial freedom at home.

question: What is the main purpose of adolescent counseling corners in primary health centers?

options.A: Providing a safe space for youths to seek guidance on emotional struggles
options.B: Isolating sick children from the rest of the community
options.C: Providing mandatory legal representation for arrested teenagers
options.D: Holding young offenders in secure custody awaiting court trials

explanation: You got it! Counseling corners offer teenagers a confidential place to talk through stress and peer pressure before things get out of hand.

question: What is a key part of effective palliative communication?

options.A: Avoiding all discussions about death
options.B: Rushing through explanations to save time
options.C: Making decisions without consulting the family
options.D: Active listening to patient and family concerns

explanation: Listening is our greatest nursing tool. When we truly listen, we build trust and make sure our care matches what the patient and family really want.

question: Which parasite forms tough outer shells (cysts) that survive normal chlorine treatment in water?

options.A: Giardia lamblia
options.B: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Giardia is a stubborn protozoan that builds protective cysts. These cysts help it survive tough conditions and shrug off standard amounts of chlorine in water treatment.

question: Which vaccine directly helps prevent a leading cause of childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.B: Hepatitis B vaccine
options.C: BCG tuberculosis vaccine
options.D: Rotavirus vaccine

explanation: Prevention is key! The rotavirus vaccine protects little ones from the most common viral bug that causes severe, dehydrating tummy bugs.

question: Why is cultural awareness especially important for rehabilitation nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: It speeds up the pharmacological action of prescribed drugs
options.B: It replaces the need for standard clinical assessments
options.C: It is required by international hospital accreditation bodies
options.D: It helps nurses adapt care plans to fit the patient's home environment and beliefs

explanation: Understanding local traditions and family structures ensures that rehabilitation goals are realistic and culturally acceptable to the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which workplace strategy shows that a hospital truly cares about long-term staff motivation?

options.A: Sponsoring specialty certifications and clear career ladders
options.B: Lowering entry-level salaries to save money for equipment
options.C: Reducing annual vacation days to increase bedside coverage
options.D: Eliminating all staff meetings to maximize shift hours

explanation: When a hospital helps you grow your skills and gives you clear paths to climb higher, you feel valued and ready to stay!

question: A depressed patient has lost ten pounds, looks pale, and is fatigued. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Assume the weight loss is normal for depression and take no action
options.B: Perform a comprehensive nutritional assessment including a diet history and labs
options.C: Recommend an intense physical fitness gym membership to build muscle
options.D: Tell the patient to immediately start eating three large meals a day

explanation: Well done! A structured assessment helps us uncover specific nutritional deficits and physical health risks.

question: An elderly patient reports poor appetite, trouble chewing, and losing weight without trying. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A sudden increase in daily physical growth velocity
options.B: An allergic reaction to drinking clean tap water
options.C: An excessive desire to run marathon races every week
options.D: Age-related dental challenges and a reduced appetite

explanation: As people get older, dental issues, changes in taste, and lower appetite often make eating tougher, putting them at risk of poor nutrition.

question: In community health nursing, what do we mean by a "food taboo"?

options.A: A cultural rule against eating certain foods
options.B: A government law controlling food prices
options.C: A medical prescription for weight loss
options.D: An allergic reaction to specific meals

explanation: A food taboo is simply a cultural or religious rule that says 'no' to eating certain edible items. You'll see this often in community postings!

question: A patient is admitted with suspected lymphoma. What is the most common early physical sign a nurse expects to find?

options.A: Severe skin rashes over the tummy
options.B: Painless, enlarged lymph nodes in the neck
options.C: Complete paralysis of both legs
options.D: Bleeding gums and sudden nosebleeds

explanation: Keep an eye out for this: the earliest and most common sign is a lump in the neck that swells up without causing any pain.

question: What happens in the kidneys during cystinuria to cause stone formation?

options.A: Rapid enzymatic breakdown of calcium in the glomerulus
options.B: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of specific amino acids
options.C: Reduced hepatic production of filtering enzymes
options.D: Excessive dietary intake of sulfur-containing proteins

explanation: Think of the kidneys like a recycling plant! In cystinuria, a little genetic mix-up stops the kidneys from reabsorbing certain amino acids back into the body. This causes cystine to build up in the urine and form stones. You've got this!

question: Where are the developing egg follicles primarily housed within the ovary?

options.A: The outer cortex
options.B: The fallopian infundibulum
options.C: The broad ligament
options.D: The inner medulla

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains the ovarian follicles in various stages of development. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of using an arterial line instead of a standard blood pressure cuff?

options.A: It automatically delivers intravenous fluids when pressure drops
options.B: It measures the exact amount of urine produced by the kidneys
options.C: It provides continuous, real-time blood pressure readings
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of infection and bleeding

explanation: An arterial line gives beat-by-beat blood pressure updates, which is super helpful for unstable patients whose numbers change fast.

question: Why might a nurse mistakenly refuse or delay PAC care due to legal fears?

options.A: Absence of any regulatory guidelines from the Nursing Council
options.B: Confusion between performing an abortion and treating its emergency complications
options.C: Strict hospital policies requiring police clearance for all emergency admissions
options.D: Lack of basic nursing equipment in rural health clinics

explanation: Some providers get scared, mistakenly thinking that treating post-abortion complications makes them an accomplice to an illegal act. Remember: treating complications is saving a life!

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

options.A: Generate rapid electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.B: Transport oxygen molecules from the lungs to body tissues
options.C: Filter waste products directly out of the bloodstream
options.D: Act as chemical messengers to regulate target organs

explanation: Think of hormones as chemical text messages sent through the blood to tell different organs what to do. You've got this!

question: Why do public health organizations strongly support male circumcision in many regions?

options.A: It stops the natural production of testosterone
options.B: It permanently eliminates the need for personal hygiene
options.C: It completely cures all forms of urinary tract infections
options.D: It helps reduce the transmission of HIV and other infections

explanation: Great job! Medical studies show that male circumcision significantly lowers the risk of contracting HIV and certain other sexually transmitted infections, making it a key public health tool.

question: Which route for measuring body temperature gives the closest reading to core body heat?

options.A: Axillary
options.B: Rectal
options.C: Oral
options.D: Tympanic

explanation: Correct! Rectal temperatures measure heat deep inside the body cavity, making them the most accurate reflection of core temperature.

question: Where do most microbes found in the air come from?

options.A: Chemical reactions between sunlight and vehicle exhaust
options.B: Purely from indoor sterile laboratory equipment
options.C: They multiply and live permanently in the upper atmosphere
options.D: Soil, water, plants, and human or animal activities

explanation: Correct! Microbes aren't actually born in the sky. They get swept up from the ground, water, or living things around us.

question: What do the blood vessels in your skin do when your body temperature gets too high and you need to cool down?

options.A: They thicken permanently
options.B: They vasodilate
options.C: They collapse entirely
options.D: They vasoconstrict

explanation: You're right! They vasodilate (open wider) to bring more warm blood close to the surface, letting excess body heat escape into the air.

question: In simple terms, what does 'demand' mean when we talk about health services?

options.A: The total amount of care that patients want and can use
options.B: The cost of buying medical equipment from abroad
options.C: The total number of doctors in a government hospital
options.D: The maximum number of beds a health center can hold

explanation: You've got this! Demand simply means the healthcare services people need and are able to access. Think of it as the care patients are asking for and using.

question: What is a simple way for a nurse to spot early signs of distress in a teen client?

options.A: Measuring their exact height and weight on a growth chart
options.B: Checking their academic transcripts from school records
options.C: Testing their blood for abnormal electrolyte imbalances
options.D: Asking about changes in their daily sleep patterns and mood

explanation: Spot on! Sudden shifts in sleep or mood are classic signs that a young person might be going through emotional distress or depression. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the main difference between an 'output' and an 'outcome' in advocacy?

options.A: Outputs measure financial costs, while outcomes measure staff attendance
options.B: Outputs happen after the project, while outcomes happen before the project
options.C: Outputs measure activities done, while outcomes measure actual results achieved
options.D: Outputs are qualitative stories, while outcomes are strictly numerical charts

explanation: Think of outputs as what you *did* (like handing out 100 flyers), and outcomes as the actual *change* that happened because of it (like more people getting vaccinated).

question: What is it called when a drug is excreted in bile, absorbed from the gut, and returned to the bloodstream in a continuous loop?

options.A: Enterohepatic recirculation
options.B: Active tubular secretion
options.C: First-pass metabolism
options.D: Glomerular filtration

explanation: Think of enterohepatic recirculation as a recycling loop between the liver and the gut. It bounces the drug back and forth, making the medicine stay active in the body much longer.

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness?

options.A: To ensure the mother pays all hospital bills in advance
options.B: To completely eliminate any need for hospital visits
options.C: To reduce delays in getting emergency care during childbirth
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on a specific weekday

explanation: Correct! Planning ahead with transport and funds stops dangerous delays when things get critical during labor.

question: Why might ethical rules stop a nurse researcher from using an experimental design for certain topics?

options.A: Experimental designs always cost more money than hospitals have
options.B: Ethical committees only approve studies written in a foreign language
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions if a design is experimental
options.D: Researchers cannot intentionally expose human patients to harm

explanation: Patient safety always comes first! If an experiment could put someone at risk, ethics boards require us to use safer, observational designs instead.

question: What is an important safety tip for any patient taking a medication that causes drowsiness?

options.A: Exercise vigorously right after each dose.
options.B: Take the medication only on an empty stomach.
options.C: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery.
options.D: Stop drinking all fluids during the daytime.

explanation: Drowsy meds slow down reflexes. Always remind patients to avoid driving or working with heavy machines until they know how the drug affects them.

question: Why are antibiotics prescribed as part of treatment for some peptic ulcers?

options.A: Directly neutralizing excess hydrochloric acid in the gut
options.B: Blocking histamine receptors on gastric parietal cells
options.C: Coating the stomach wall to prevent physical irritation
options.D: Eradicating Helicobacter pylori bacterial infections

explanation: Many ulcers are caused by a stubborn bacteria called H. pylori. Clearing it out with antibiotics helps the ulcer heal completely.

question: How do correlational studies usually help prepare for future clinical trials?

options.A: By replacing the need for any human participants in the lab
options.B: By proving beyond doubt that a treatment cures a disease
options.C: By showing that a relationship exists to justify further research
options.D: By randomly assigning patients to control and treatment groups

explanation: Brilliant! Finding a solid connection in a correlational study gives scientists the green light to invest time and money into bigger experiments.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a needle count is incorrect?

options.A: Inform the surgeon and stop wound closure
options.B: Clean up the operating room and send the patient away
options.C: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask if they feel pain
options.D: Write an incident report and leave the theatre

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Never let a wound be closed when a count is wrong. Always speak up right away. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which scenario is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: Getting infected with malaria from a mosquito bite during the rainy season
options.B: Catching a cold after touching a shared pen that an infected coworker used
options.C: Developing a wound infection from direct contact with a draining sore
options.D: Inhaling large respiratory droplets expelled by someone coughing nearby

explanation: The shared pen acts as a fomite, transferring the virus indirectly from the coworker's hand to the new host's hand. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h4)

question: In the famous Swiss Cheese Model, what do the holes in the cheese slices represent?

options.A: Active weaknesses or gaps in safety defenses
options.B: Natural symptoms of a progressing illness
options.C: Successful steps in medication administration
options.D: Deliberate criminal acts committed by staff

explanation: Think of the holes as little gaps or weaknesses in our hospital safety checks that can occasionally let an error slip through.

question: Which seasonal weather condition in northern Nigeria is famous for triggering outbreaks of cerebrospinal meningitis?

options.A: The dry harmattan season
options.B: The cold December nights
options.C: The heavy rainy season
options.D: The coastal flooding period

explanation: Well done! The dry harmattan brings dust and low humidity that irritate our airways, making meningitis outbreaks more common during this time.

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Storing excess kilocalories for times of fasting
options.B: Regulating fluid balance and nerve transmission
options.C: Acting as primary structural units for muscle fibers
options.D: Providing the main source of daily cellular energy

explanation: Spot on! Sodium and potassium are key electrolytes that keep our fluids balanced and help nerves send signals to muscles.

question: What do government rehabilitation programs usually provide for displaced or vulnerable people?

options.A: Exemption from all federal and state laws
options.B: Vocational skills training and temporary shelter
options.C: Free commercial real estate deeds
options.D: Mandatory relocation to a foreign country

explanation: You got it! Rehabilitation programs help stabilize vulnerable people by giving them a safe place to stay and practical skills to stand on their own feet.

question: Why do nurses use standard screening tools like the Patient Health Questionnaire in clinical practice?

options.A: To quantify and measure depression symptom severity
options.B: To measure blood levels of neurotransmitters
options.C: To test physical strength and muscular endurance
options.D: To diagnose specific neurological brain disorders

explanation: Exactly! Screening tools give us a clear, structured way to score how severe a patient's depressive symptoms are so we can track their progress.

question: A patient is brought to the ward in a deep coma after a severe head injury. Which nursing action is best to prevent stiff joints?

options.A: Doing regular passive range of motion exercises
options.B: Encouraging the client to squeeze rubber balls daily
options.C: Tying all four limbs tightly to the bed rails
options.D: Putting heavy sandbags on the hands and feet

explanation: Brilliant! An unconscious client cannot move on their own, so scheduled passive range of motion keeps their joints mobile and safe.

question: Which group of medications helps the body get rid of extra fluid through urine?

options.A: Antipyretics
options.B: Analgesics
options.C: Diuretics
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: Correct! Diuretics (often called water pills) trick the kidneys into flushing out extra salt and water, which brings the swelling down.

question: What is a major challenge when you take a successful small test and try to use it across a whole hospital department?

options.A: The original nurses will refuse to share their secrets with others
options.B: Patients will automatically reject any change that originated outside their room
options.C: Different shifts may face unique conditions that cause the workflow to struggle
options.D: The hospital will immediately run out of paper charting supplies

explanation: What works smoothly during a quiet morning shift might totally jam up during a crazy night shift! Always expect to adapt when expanding your tests.

question: What is one of the main responsibilities of community health workers when it comes to post-natal care?

options.A: Performing major surgical repairs for tears
options.B: Delivering babies in primary operating theatres
options.C: Conducting home visits and tracking immunizations
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for severe sepsis

explanation: Community health workers are fantastic bridges to the community. They visit homes to make sure babies get their vaccines and moms are recovering nicely.

question: What is the primary clinical role of a family planning record?

options.A: To serve as a financial receipt for services
options.B: To track client history and guide ongoing care
options.C: To provide data exclusively for government tax audits
options.D: To replace verbal communication entirely

explanation: Family planning records are designed primarily to maintain a clear history of a client's reproductive health needs to guide safe, continuous care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h1)

question: Why do health teams run mobile clinics and community outreach programs?

options.A: To train people to become certified physicians
options.B: To reach populations living far from permanent health facilities
options.C: To replace traditional hospitals permanently
options.D: To collect taxes from rural farming communities

explanation: Correct! Mobile clinics bridge the gap by taking healthcare services right to the doorsteps of remote villages that lack permanent clinics.

question: A patient with a bacterial infection wants to stop taking antibiotics after two days because they feel fine. What should you tell them?

options.A: They must double the remaining dose on the third day instead
options.B: They should save the remaining pills for a headache next week
options.C: Stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and more resistant
options.D: It is completely safe to stop once fever symptoms disappear

explanation: You got it! Always encourage patients to finish the full dose so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger.

question: Which common organism causes most vaginal and urinary tract fungal infections?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Candida species
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation: Candida species (like Candida albicans) are the usual suspects behind yeast infections in our private parts. You've got this!

question: What is the recommended maximum time window to start HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) after a needle-stick injury?

options.A: 72 hours
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 1 week

explanation: Time matters! PEP for HIV should be started as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of the exposure, to be most effective.

question: A nurse cares for a patient with a drug-resistant wound infection. Which principle guides safe nursing care?

options.A: Treating all patient blood and body fluids as infectious using standard precautions
options.B: Reusing medical equipment between patients if it looks visually clean
options.C: Stopping all hand hygiene once gloves are removed from the hands
options.D: Assuming infection control is only necessary if the patient shows a high fever

question: How do cultural misconceptions about disabilities directly impact a special child?

options.A: They motivate rapid medical diagnosis in rural clinics
options.B: They improve community volunteer participation
options.C: They often lead families to hide the child away due to shame or fear
options.D: They guarantee immediate government scholarship awards

explanation: Superstitious beliefs and heavy stigma can cause families to conceal children, keeping them away from the medical and social support they deserve.

question: Which preparation is specifically designed as a liquid instillation into the rectum?

options.A: Transdermal patch
options.B: Enema
options.C: Sublingual tablet
options.D: Suppository

question: What keeps a Foley urinary catheter securely in place inside the bladder?

options.A: Special surgical glue applied to the inner thigh skin
options.B: A tight plastic clamp attached around the external tubing
options.C: An inflated water balloon near the catheter tip
options.D: Natural suction created by the urine collection bag

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of long-term rehabilitation after a nervous system injury?

options.A: Reversing the primary neural cell death caused by the initial crash
options.B: Helping the client adapt to permanent physical disabilities
options.C: Supporting family members through emotional counseling
options.D: Providing physical therapy to prevent muscle contractures

question: Blood is soaking right through the gauze on a leg wound you are pressing. What should you do next?

options.A: Remove the soaked gauze to inspect the cut
options.B: Stop pressing entirely and prep for surgery
options.C: Rinse the wound with sterile saline
options.D: Add more gauze pads right on top of the old ones and keep pressing

explanation: Never take off the first layer of gauze—you'll tear away the tiny new clots trying to form. Just pile more on top and keep holding pressure!

question: What is the proper term for the biological process of making mature sperm cells during male puberty?

options.A: Spermatogenesis
options.B: Oogenesis
options.C: Gluconeogenesis
options.D: Glycolysis

explanation: Awesome! 'Spermatogenesis' simply means the creation (-genesis) of sperm, fueled by FSH and testosterone.

question: What feeding advice should a nurse give to a mother whose baby has acute diarrhea?

options.A: Stop all milk feeds for at least 48 hours to rest the gut
options.B: Withhold all food until the diarrhea stops completely
options.C: Replace breastmilk with plain water and sugar
options.D: Continue breastfeeding frequently throughout the illness

explanation: Never starve the gut! Breastfeeding gives the baby essential comfort, immune support, and nutrients to help them recover faster.

question: Why must acids and alkaline substances (bases) never be stored right next to each other?

options.A: Mixing them can cause violent reactions, heat, or toxic gas
options.B: Alkaline fumes destroy the paper labels on acid containers
options.C: They will neutralize each other and become expensive perfume
options.D: Acids make alkaline bottles shrink and leak everywhere

explanation: Spot on! Acids and bases react strongly when they meet, often releasing dangerous heat, splashes, or poisonous fumes. Keeping them apart keeps everyone safe.

question: How does public health differ from regular clinical (curative) medicine?

options.A: Curative medicine focuses on individuals, while public health focuses on communities.
options.B: Public health ignores infectious diseases completely.
options.C: Clinical medicine relies entirely on environmental sanitation.
options.D: Curative medicine is only practiced in rural areas.

explanation: You've got it! Clinical practice is all about treating the single sick person in front of you, whereas public health cares for the health status of the whole group.

question: Which of these is a daily operational duty in a running health clinic?

options.A: Designing new national health policies in the capital city
options.B: Maintaining proper cold-chain storage for vaccines and supplies
options.C: Conducting the final statistical evaluation of the program
options.D: Securing international grants for future research studies

explanation: Day-to-day operations involve practical care, like making sure vaccines stay cold and clinic traffic flows smoothly.

question: How should emergency stock items on a ward be managed differently from regular supplies?

options.A: Ordered only once a year to cut down on paperwork
options.B: Checked daily and replaced immediately after any use
options.C: Stored in a locked room away from all nursing staff
options.D: Kept in open corridors for easy public access

explanation: Emergency items must be ready at a moment's notice, requiring daily checks and instant replenishment if used. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: What happens to the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It increases significantly
options.B: It stays completely unchanged
options.C: It drops to near zero
options.D: It fluctuates every hour

question: What is sampling bias?

options.A: The deliberate refusal of a patient to answer survey questions
options.B: A systematic flaw where the selection process favors certain outcomes
options.C: An error made by a laboratory technician reading a blood test
options.D: The natural difference between a sample result and the population

explanation: Correct! Sampling bias happens when our selection method accidentally leans too much toward one side, so the sample doesn't truly reflect reality.

question: What is a major benefit of connecting a visually impaired patient with a peer support group?

options.A: Diagnosing the underlying cause of their eye disease
options.B: Providing free medical treatments and prescription drugs
options.C: Sharing practical coping strategies and reducing isolation
options.D: Replacing the need for professional nursing home care

explanation: Spot on! Talking to others going through similar experiences helps patients feel less alone and gives them great everyday tips for living with low vision.

question: Which main chemical in tobacco makes it so addictive?

options.A: Ammonia
options.B: Tar
options.C: Carbon monoxide
options.D: Nicotine

explanation: Nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco that hooks the brain and drives the urge to keep smoking. You've got this!

question: Why is goal congruence beneficial for a healthcare facility?

options.A: It allows the hospital to operate without any nurses
options.B: Staff members become more productive when hospital success helps them reach their personal goals
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never complain about food
options.D: It completely removes the need to pay staff salaries

explanation: When helping the hospital succeed also helps you achieve your own dreams (like promotions or training), you naturally feel more motivated and do your best work!

question: Which hormone does the pineal gland release to help you sleep?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: You nailed it! The pineal gland pumps out melatonin when it gets dark to help your body wind down for sleep.

question: What is the primary tool used in tele-nursing to deliver care?

options.A: Information and communication technologies
options.B: Surgical instruments and sterile trays
options.C: Laboratory reagents and microscopy
options.D: Manual blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes

explanation: Tele-nursing relies fundamentally on electronic communication tools like phones and computers to reach patients remotely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses spend time educating the public?

options.A: To replace formal school teachers in local primary classrooms
options.B: To empower individuals and groups with knowledge to prevent illness
options.C: To test public speaking skills during routine ward rounds
options.D: To fulfill mandatory administrative writing quotas

explanation: Spot on! Education is one of our most powerful tools. When people understand how diseases spread and how to live healthily, they can take charge of their own wellbeing.

question: A community health nurse is assigned to a quarantine camp. Which combination of tasks forms her core daily responsibility?

options.A: Enforcing court orders, arresting rulebreakers, and guarding the perimeter gate
options.B: Importing medical equipment and managing the national budget
options.C: Diagnosing new viral strains using advanced laboratory genome sequencing
options.D: Monitoring temperatures, providing health education, and offering emotional support

explanation: The nurse's core role centers on clinical monitoring, patient education, and psychosocial care within the facility. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: What is the protective protein shell enclosing a virus's genetic material called?

options.A: Flagella
options.B: Spore
options.C: Peptidoglycan
options.D: Capsid

explanation: The capsid serves as armor protecting the fragile viral DNA or RNA. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which imaging test is generally considered the best for viewing tissue death and fluid collections in acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Standard chest X-ray
options.B: Basic abdominal ultrasound
options.C: CT scan with contrast
options.D: Electrocardiogram strip

explanation: You got it! A contrast CT gives doctors the clearest pictures to spot inflammation, dead tissue, and hidden pockets of fluid around the pancreas.

question: Where do nurses mostly interact with patients regarding reproductive health prevention?

options.A: Exclusively in legislative chambers writing health policies
options.B: At the frontline of both community outreach and clinical care settings
options.C: Only within pharmaceutical manufacturing laboratories
options.D: Solely inside international boardrooms managing NGO budgets

explanation: Exactly! Nurses are right there on the frontlines—out in the communities and inside the clinics—making prevention happen every day.

question: What is the primary function of plasmin during the healing process?

options.A: It breaks down and dissolves the fibrin clot

options.C: It causes the initial vascular spasm in injured vessels
options.D: It converts inactive prothrombin into active thrombin

explanation: Plasmin is the active enzyme responsible for digesting fibrin strands so the body can clear away old, unneeded clots. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: A post-abortion patient suddenly develops severe chest pain and shortness of breath on the ward. What should you do right away?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.B: Discharging the patient home for rest
options.C: Requesting immediate consultation with the appropriate medical specialist
options.D: Telling the patient that chest pain is normal after an abortion

explanation: Chest pain and trouble breathing are red flags. Unstable symptoms like these mean you need to call for a specialist review right away.

question: Why are families who rely only on subsistence farming at risk of malnutrition?

options.A: Subsistence farmers are legally forbidden from eating their own crops.
options.B: Growing food at home causes chronic fatigue in children.
options.C: Home-grown food contains zero vitamins or minerals.
options.D: A failed harvest from drought or pests directly removes their food supply.

explanation: You got it. If bad weather or pests ruin the crops, these families lose both their meals and their fallback income all at once.

question: Why do children have different nutritional needs compared to adults?

options.A: Children require fewer calories per kilogram of body weight
options.B: Children do not need micronutrients until puberty begins
options.C: Adults have higher metabolic demands than growing children
options.D: Children are actively building new tissue and growing rapidly

explanation: Spot on! Growing kids need extra fuel and building blocks because their bones, muscles, and organs are developing fast. You've got this!

question: Which germs are the most common causes of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Candida albicans and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae

question: How does time-driven activity-based costing make hospital budgeting better?

question: What is a common myth people believe about using digital tools in nursing practice?

options.A: People believe computers can completely replace all doctors and nurses.
options.B: People think digital materials can only be used by illiterate community members.
options.C: People assume mobile phones do not require any battery power to operate.
options.D: People believe digital tools completely replace traditional face-to-face nursing contact.

explanation: Digital tools are awesome helpers, but they can never replace the warmth and trust of real human touch and face-to-face nursing care.

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of fake nutrition advice?

options.A: Advising patients to eat a balanced variety of all food groups
options.B: Publishing raw data from randomized and controlled clinical trials
options.C: Requiring regular blood tests supervised by a registered dietitian

explanation: If one simple tea or supplement claims to cure everything from malaria to headaches, run the other way! Real medicine doesn't work that way.

question: What is a common cause of diarrhea when a patient is receiving tube feeds at home?

options.A: Elevating the bed during the feeding
options.B: Keeping the room temperature too warm
options.C: Infusing the formula too rapidly
options.D: Flushing the tube with plain sterile water

question: A nurse is caring for a patient from a remote mountainous region with high rates of goiter. What public health program should the nurse support?

options.A: Teaching deep-sea fishing techniques
options.B: Introducing desert camel farming

question: Why is it important to involve community members at every step of an advocacy project?

options.A: It prevents government officials from visiting the health center

options.C: It ensures that the nurse receives financial compensation from villagers

question: What is a major economic driver pushing children onto the streets in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding for public primary education

options.C: Abundant social welfare support for large families
options.D: Widespread household poverty and unemployment

question: What is a primary treatment goal for clients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any family involvement

question: During an emergency cesarean section, a surgeon tells the team to skip the safety timeout because every second counts. How should the circulating nurse respond?

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving a patient a new biological medication?

options.A: Ensuring the medication is stored in direct sunlight at room temperature

options.C: Assuming all biological products are completely safe from side effects

question: How do safety checklists contribute to quality patient care in clinical practice?

options.A: They shorten the operating time for emergency surgeries

options.D: They prevent the omission of critical steps during complex procedures

question: What is a crucial piece of advice a nurse should give a patient starting daily hormone pills?

options.A: Double your dose whenever you feel stressed or tired
options.B: Never stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the pills once your blood test results return to normal

question: Why is knowing the chain of infection so helpful for nurses?

options.C: It proves which specific antibiotic will cure the patient

question: What is one of the most important goals of nursing education when it comes to menstrual health?

question: What is the main job of glucocorticoids (like cortisol) released by the middle layer of the adrenal cortex?

question: In the chain of infection, what do we call the cozy home base where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Susceptible host

options.D: Infectious agent

question: A labouring mum has strong contractions, but the baby's head is quite large. What natural process helps the foetal skull pass through her pelvis?

question: Where does the scrub nurse position themselves during an operation?

question: Why is avoiding all medications during pregnancy sometimes dangerous?

options.B: The placenta will release toxins if no drugs are present in the blood

question: Which nursing advice helps prevent burnout in a gifted child with a packed daily schedule?

question: Who opened the first birth control clinic in the United States in 1916?

question: A community health nurse wants to reduce head injuries among local commercial motorcycle riders. What is the best step to take?

question: How often should you check the circulation and nerves (neurovascular status) of a limb in skin traction?

question: What is the main reason kidney (renal) clearance slows down as people get older?

question: How do daily community health records help with national health planning in Nigeria?

question: Which of these is a very common mental health challenge for survivors of ongoing abuse?

question: Which of the following is a major drawback or limitation of using research checklists?

question: A patient has an autoimmune condition where their insulin-making cells are destroyed. What lab finding is most likely?

question: What does having 'psychological safety' mean for a nursing team?

options.C: Wards are kept completely quiet at night to reduce stress

question: When is the correct time to document that you have given a medication?

question: What is the sympathetic nervous system mainly doing while your bladder is filling up?

question: Aside from treating cuts and bruises, what was another big focus for early industrial nurses?

question: A community experiences a sudden outbreak of severe diarrhea linked to contaminated street food. What is the most appropriate regulatory response?

question: Which post-procedure sign means you need to call the medical team right away?

question: Why do people often compare a research design to an architect's drawing?

question: What does the abbreviation 'gtt' mean in medication administration?

question: What is the best first step for a nurse assessing a suspected victim of forced marriage?

question: Why would you want to conduct a key informant interview with a respected local elder?

question: What is the medical term for a young girl's very first menstrual period?

question: A patient is given a drug that stimulates beta-2 receptors. What body change do you expect?

question: Which statement represents objective, professional documentation in a health record?

question: What is the main purpose of genetic counseling for families affected by these disorders?

options.A: To provide daily physical therapy for weakened muscles

options.C: To perform surgical procedures that repair damaged genes
options.D: To explain inheritance risks and guide family planning decisions

explanation: Genetic counselors help families understand how a condition is passed down and discuss testing options for other relatives.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should figure out before teaching a patient at home?

options.A: How the patient and family process information
options.B: The exact brand of television in the living room
options.C: The cost of the patient's home insurance policy
options.D: How many bedrooms the house contains

explanation: Always check their literacy level, language preferences, and how they learn best so your teaching actually makes sense to them.

question: Which type of health need is decided by healthcare professionals using expert standards?

options.A: Felt need
options.B: Normative need
options.C: Expressed need
options.D: Comparative need

explanation: You got it! "Normative" comes from norms or standards. These are the needs experts spot based on professional guidelines and research.

question: Which bone is located at the very back of a baby's skull?

options.A: The occipital bone
options.B: The frontal bone
options.C: The sphenoid bone
options.D: The temporal bone

explanation: Spot on! The occipital bone sits at the back and forms the lower base and rear part of the skull.

question: What does 'overflow incontinence' mean when talking about urinary retention?

options.A: Passing large amounts of clear urine every hour
options.B: Total loss of bladder control due to a spinal injury
options.C: Leaking small amounts of urine because the bladder is too full
options.D: Involuntary loss of urine only during physical exercise

question: When does monitoring of a community health program actually happen?

options.A: Before any assessment or planning begins
options.B: Only after the entire project has completely ended
options.C: Five years after everyone has forgotten the project
options.D: While the program is actively running

explanation: Great job! Monitoring is ongoing supervision that happens live during implementation so you can catch and fix mistakes right away.

question: A nurse leading a polio vaccination campaign notices sudden community resistance due to false rumors spread on social media. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Punish any community member who asks questions about the vaccine
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders to openly address and debunk the rumors
options.C: Ignore the rumors completely and hope the villagers forget them
options.D: Cancel the entire vaccination campaign and close the health clinic

explanation: Rumors spread fast, but trusted local voices spread clarity faster! Partnering with community leaders is the best way to calm fears and protect public health.

question: Why do many victims find it so hard to leave an abusive relationship?

options.A: Physical injuries heal completely without long-term effects
options.B: Healthcare workers advise them to remain at home
options.C: Fear, financial dependence, and isolation trap them in the relationship
options.D: They genuinely enjoy the tension-building cycle

explanation: Leaving is complicated and dangerous. Fear and a lack of financial support create huge walls that keep people stuck.

question: Which chemical messenger is mainly responsible for the brain's reward system and feelings of pleasure during drug use?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Nailed it! Dopamine is our feel-good chemical. Drugs flood the brain with it, creating an intense artificial high that tricks the reward system.

question: An HIV-positive mum looks worried and stressed about her infant feeding choices. What should be your very first step as a student nurse?

options.A: Build trust and provide a safe space to discuss her fears and questions
options.B: Tell her immediately that formula feeding is the only acceptable choice
options.C: Hand her a detailed textbook on virology and let her read independently
options.D: Involve her extended family in the discussion without her prior consent

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Always start by creating a warm, judgment-free space where she feels safe to share her worries before diving into clinical advice.

question: What is the primary difference between hypovolemic shock and cardiogenic shock?

options.A: Cardiogenic shock is caused by severe allergic reactions
options.B: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a blocked pulmonary artery
options.C: Cardiogenic shock involves heart pump failure, while hypovolemic shock involves fluid loss
options.D: Hypovolemic shock always features a very slow heart rate

explanation: In cardiogenic shock, blood volume is normal, but the heart muscle is too weak to pump it; in hypovolemic shock, the pump is fine, but volume is missing. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h4)

question: What size syringe is standard for administering an intradermal injection?

options.A: Large gravity syringe of 10 mL
options.B: Tuberculin syringe of 1 mL
options.C: Hypodermic syringe of 3 mL
options.D: Insulin syringe of 0.5 mL

explanation: A 1 mL tuberculin syringe allows accurate measurement of the very small doses used in intradermal injections. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of stock holding conventions in a nursing unit?

options.A: Reducing the salary budget of nursing staff
options.B: Increasing the number of beds in the ward
options.C: Ensuring vital supplies are available when needed
options.D: Complying with hospital architectural designs

explanation: Stock holding conventions focus mainly on making sure medical items and drugs are always ready for patient care without shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Why do body cells swell and break open during the final stages of dying?

options.A: Sodium and water rush in because cell pumps stop working
options.B: Lactic acid builds up inside blood vessels
options.C: White blood cells attack healthy tissues
options.D: Extra glucose pulls water into the cells

explanation: Without ATP, the tiny pumps that keep sodium out of cells stop working. Sodium stays inside, brings water with it, and causes the cell to swell. Great thinking!

question: Why is true informed consent sometimes difficult to achieve in strongly patriarchal settings?

options.A: Contraceptive drugs have secret side effects that cannot be explained
options.B: Medical terminology is naturally too complex for any patient to understand
options.C: Nurses are legally required to make treatment choices for female patients
options.D: Patients may be pressured by family members to follow decisions made on their behalf

explanation: In some cultures, family or spousal approval is expected for everything. This can make it tricky to ensure a patient's personal choice is truly respected and free from pressure.

question: Which organ in the body is the main workstation for breaking down most medications?

options.A: The stomach
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The pancreas

explanation: The liver is like the body's chemical factory. It uses special enzymes (the famous cytochrome P450 system) to process and break down most of the drugs we take.

question: What are the coarse hairs located inside the nasal vestibule called?

options.A: Vibrissae
options.B: Turbinates
options.C: Cilia
options.D: Microvilli

explanation: Vibrissae are the stiff, coarse hairs at the entrance of the nose that catch large bugs, dust, and debris. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Two hours after a colonoscopy, a patient's abdomen feels hard like a board and they have severe pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to pass trapped gas
options.B: Administer a strong oral laxative to clear the bowels quickly
options.C: Notify the physician immediately and keep the patient nil per os
options.D: Offer the patient a warm glass of water to soothe the stomach

explanation: A rigid, hard tummy with sharp pain is a classic red flag for a bowel perforation. Call the doctor straight away and stop all food and drinks (nil per os).

question: Why is strict sterile (aseptic) technique so important during a paracentesis?

options.A: To help the puncture site heal without a scar
options.B: To stop the patient from moving around
options.C: To make the local anesthetic work much faster
options.D: To prevent introducing bacteria into the abdomen

explanation: Keeping everything sterile ensures we don't accidentally push germs from the skin into the sterile belly cavity.

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient after inserting a retention suppository?

options.A: Drink two liters of ice-cold water within five minutes
options.B: Force an immediate bowel movement to test if it worked
options.C: Try to remain lying down and hold the medication for 15 to 30 minutes
options.D: Get up immediately and walk briskly around the hospital hallway

explanation: Giving the medication time to dissolve and absorb into the mucosal lining prevents it from being prematurely expelled. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: What sign should a nurse watch for as a delayed allergic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.B: Loss of taste on the tongue
options.C: Skin rash, hives, or itching
options.D: Temporary extra hair growth

explanation: Sometimes allergies show up hours later. Watch out for rashes, hives, or itching so you can treat them early.

question: Why do most primary brain tumors start in neuroglial cells rather than mature neurons?

options.A: Neurons lack a cell membrane to protect against damage
options.B: Glial cells do not require oxygen or glucose supply
options.C: Neurons are too small to undergo cancerous mutations
options.D: Glial cells retain the ability to divide throughout life

explanation: Mature neurons stop dividing once we grow up, but glial cells can keep dividing. Because they keep multiplying, they are much more prone to forming tumors if things go wrong.

question: To diagnose Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), how long must a patient experience excessive, hard-to-control worry?

options.A: One year
options.B: Six months
options.C: One month
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: Correct! For a GAD diagnosis, the persistent worry needs to span at least six months. Keep up the brilliant study habit!

question: A researcher targets prisoners for a risky drug trial just because they are locked up and easy to reach. Which ethical rule is being broken?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Spot on! Justice means fair selection, so vulnerable groups aren't unfairly dumped with all the riskiest studies.

question: Why might a newly graduated nurse hesitate to accept delegated duties from a senior colleague?

options.A: Fear of failure and lack of professional self-confidence
options.B: Belief that delegation is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Desire to take over the senior colleague's official management title
options.D: Preference for administrative paperwork over direct patient care

explanation: It's totally normal for fresh grads to feel nervous! Doubts usually stem from a lack of confidence and the fear of making mistakes early on.

question: Why must nurse managers review monthly financial reports?

options.A: To catch and investigate budget variances before they become major deficits
options.B: To determine which nurses should be disciplined for making mistakes
options.C: To change the medical diagnoses written in patient clinical charts
options.D: To calculate the annual bonus for the hospital's chief executive officer

explanation: Monthly reviews allow managers to spot overspending early and take corrective action. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary function of planning in nursing management?

options.A: It is used strictly to discipline underperforming ward staff.
options.B: It replaces the need for daily shift handovers and reports.
options.C: It serves as the foundational starting point before organizing or directing.
options.D: It focuses exclusively on purchasing hospital medical equipment.

explanation: Planning comes first in the management cycle because you cannot organize or direct staff without a clear goal. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do we generally avoid giving live vaccines to pregnant women?

options.A: Live vaccines deactivate automatically in pregnant bloodstreams
options.B: Hormonal changes turn live viruses into strong bacteria
options.C: Pregnant women always develop permanent immunity instantly
options.D: There is a theoretical risk of harming the developing fetus

explanation: Live vaccines contain weakened germs that might pose risks during pregnancy, so we prefer using safe, inactivated options instead.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent cross-contamination in the fridge?

options.A: Storing raw meat on the top shelf above fresh vegetables
options.B: Cleaning refrigerator shelves regularly with sanitizer
options.C: Keeping raw poultry separate from ready-to-eat salads
options.D: Using tightly sealed containers for all raw animal products

explanation: Never put raw meat on top! Juices can drip down onto your veggies, causing nasty contamination.

question: What is a major job of minerals like calcium in the human body?

options.A: Insulating internal organs against cold temperatures
options.B: Building strong bones and transmitting nerve signals
options.C: Providing the bulk needed for regular bowel movements
options.D: Serving as the primary energy source for running

explanation: Minerals do heavy lifting behind the scenes. Calcium builds strong bones and teeth, and helps your nerves and muscles communicate smoothly!

question: Why is fat stored around the abdomen (apple shape) more risky for health than fat on the hips (gynoid shape)?

options.A: It places excessive mechanical weight directly on the knee joints
options.B: It indicates deep visceral fat surrounding vital metabolic organs
options.C: It causes rapid loss of skeletal muscle mass in the lower limbs
options.D: It prevents the proper expansion of the rib cage during deep breathing

explanation: Spot on! Belly fat (visceral fat) sits right around our major organs and pumps out inflammatory substances that drive up heart disease and diabetes risks.

question: Which condition is a major safety risk specifically related to maternity care?

options.A: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.B: Chronic knee osteoarthritis
options.C: Diabetic foot ulceration
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Excessive bleeding after childbirth is one of the leading preventable causes of maternal mortality worldwide, requiring strict monitoring and rapid response. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: If a doctor tells you a patient has a mild stage of endometriosis, what does that tell you about her pain?

options.A: Pain levels increase in direct proportion to the amount of scar tissue
options.B: Surgical stage does not reliably predict the severity of the patient's pain
options.C: Patients with stage IV disease always experience the worst pelvic pain
options.D: Patients with stage I disease never require strong pain medication

explanation: Surprise! A patient with just a tiny bit of endometriosis can be in agonizing pain, while another with widespread patches might feel very little. Pain and staging don't always match.

question: What happens when a drug that slows down liver enzymes is taken with another medication?

options.A: The second drug is excreted through the kidneys within minutes
options.B: The second drug binds more tightly to plasma proteins in the blood
options.C: The second drug breaks down slower, increasing the risk of toxicity
options.D: The second drug absorbs much faster from the stomach lining

explanation: If the liver's processing speed is slowed down, the companion drug hangs around longer instead of clearing out. Over time, it builds up in the blood to levels that can become toxic.

question: What is the primary reason for the physiological anemia seen during pregnancy?

options.A: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass
options.B: Red blood cells are actively destroyed at a much faster rate
options.C: Frequent blood tests deplete the iron stores of the mother
options.D: Dietary iron is completely blocked from being absorbed in the gut

explanation: Because plasma volume expands much faster and larger than the actual red blood cell count, the blood becomes more diluted, which registers as a lower hemoglobin concentration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: Why is getting input from the family so crucial during a mental health assessment for these conditions?

options.A: Nurses are not allowed to speak directly with the affected patient
options.B: Patients may lack the insight to recognize their own behavioral changes
options.C: Patient memories always remain completely accurate throughout the illness
options.D: Family members are legally required to answer all diagnostic quizzes

explanation: Well reasoned! As the brain declines, patients often can't see their own mental changes, so family stories give nurses the true picture. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h4)

question: Your patient has dry skin, blurry vision, can't pass urine, and seems quite confused after taking an unknown drug. What toxidrome are they showing?

options.A: Anticholinergic
options.B: Sedative-hypnotic
options.C: Sympathomimetic
options.D: Cholinergic

explanation: Think of anticholinergic drugs as drying up all the body's moisture—hence the dry skin, urinary retention, and blurry vision, plus a confused mind!

question: What is usually the main cause behind an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Taking a medication past its expiry date
options.B: Inherited genetic differences in metabolism
options.C: Accidental double dosing by the patient
options.D: Mixing the drug with dairy products

explanation: Often, it all comes down to genetics! Everyone's body breaks down drugs slightly differently because of the genes they inherited.

question: What does 'external validity' deal with?

options.A: How fast data goes into the hospital computer
options.B: How well patients understand their consent forms
options.C: Whether the study results can apply to other patients in the real world
options.D: How accurate the thermometers are in the laboratory

explanation: External validity asks: 'If this worked in a tiny research lab, will it also work for our patients out here on the busy hospital wards?'

question: What is the main purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: Conducting laboratory research on new medications
options.B: Treating individual patients in hospital wards
options.C: Tracking health data to guide planning and action
options.D: Managing hospital financial budgets and staff

explanation: Surveillance focuses on collecting and analyzing population health data so authorities can take proper action to protect the public. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: A client is finding it hard to stick to a new meal plan. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Scold the client for lacking discipline and willpower
options.B: Adjust the plan to include small, realistic, and affordable changes
options.C: Insist the client eat only bland hospital-style food
options.D: Discontinue all nutritional counseling immediately

explanation: Wonderful nursing approach! Small, realistic steps help clients build lasting habits without feeling overwhelmed.

question: Why should nurses check on the emotional well-being of brothers and sisters in a family affected by cerebral palsy?

options.A: Parents usually ignore the affected child to focus entirely on healthy siblings
options.B: Siblings must legally take over financial caregiving once they turn eighteen
options.C: Siblings are at high risk of developing cerebral palsy themselves
options.D: Siblings can experience feelings of neglect, stress, or added responsibilities

explanation: A chronic condition affects the whole household. Siblings often need emotional support to handle changing roles and big feelings.

question: What happens in the body when Beta-2 adrenergic receptors are stimulated?

options.A: Relaxation of smooth muscle in the airways
options.B: Decrease in overall heart rate and force
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: Increased production of digestive fluids

question: What is the main job of a pessary when treating pelvic organ prolapse?

options.A: To destroy abnormal fungal cells causing severe vaginitis
options.B: To permanently seal a vesicovaginal fistula
options.C: To physically support prolapsed pelvic organs inside the vagina
options.D: To replace lost estrogen in postmenopausal women

explanation: You're doing great! A pessary is a supportive device placed inside the vagina to hold dropped pelvic organs right where they belong.

question: Why must patients take their hormone replacement medication for life?

options.A: Stopping the drug suddenly cures the underlying condition
options.B: Glands regenerate faster if they do not receive pills
options.C: Medications build up toxic stores in the liver over time
options.D: The body cannot naturally make up for the missing hormone

explanation: Since the gland can't fix itself or make the hormone anymore, the patient needs ongoing help from daily medicine to stay healthy.

question: Why are finger foods often recommended for patients in the middle to late stages of dementia?

options.A: They make eating easier for patients who struggle with utensils
options.B: They eliminate the need for any supervision during meal times
options.C: They guarantee the patient will consume more protein than meat stews
options.D: They prevent the patient from ever dropping crumbs on the floor

explanation: Using forks and spoons can become too complex. Finger foods help patients feed themselves independently and keep up their nutrition.

question: What is the golden rule of ethics when doing research with human beings?

options.A: Ensuring participants pay for taking part in the study
options.B: Keeping the true purpose of the study a secret forever
options.C: Publishing the real names of every patient in the local newspaper
options.D: Protecting participants from harm and respecting their autonomy

explanation: You nailed it! Patient safety, voluntary choice, and dignity always come first—before any research data.

question: When assessing a postpartum mother at home, what does a firm uterine fundus indicate?

options.A: A delayed healing process of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: An abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity
options.C: Effective muscle contraction to prevent excessive bleeding
options.D: Complete closure of the cervix back to normal size
